description: Bean qou-prjo. Resolves the gauge under-determination reported by PR #4798 for the transverse NA-Stokes surface-curvature pairing on the deuteron (σ₁³/trefoil) Seifert surface. Two corpus conventions — the germ (def:germ-commutator-q-curvature: δq is a germ-level increment of q, i.e. the logarithmic q-derivative) and the transport (Yekutieli path-ordering + Seifert bands↔letters) — fix both gauges. The q-derivative germs are q-independent constants (H−2E, −H); their commutator F_q = −4E is a pure root vector of the ρ(σ₁) torus with Ad(σ₁)F_q = −q²F_q, so every transported curvature is a scalar multiple of one element and the pairing vanishes for EVERY intersection form and EVERY handle-exponent assignment (checked exhaustively over 49 pairs). Determined c₂ = 0, not the g₂ ≈ 1.0087 that would close the deuteron. scope-(b) structural exclusion restricted to single-generator (2,L)-torus channels; A ≥ 3 multi-generator remains scope-(a) open. Lean (sorry-free): QOU/MassTheory/GermRootVectorGaugeFixing.lean. 0 free parameters; g₂ used only for the post-hoc comparison, never inverted.

parameters.transport_convention: Yekutieli ordered partial product along the braid word

caveats: scope-(b) STRUCTURAL EXCLUSION restricted to single-generator (2,L)-torus channels. Cited invariant: the Ad(rho(sigma_1))-eigenvector property of the germ q-curvature. Multi-generator words (A >= 3) are NOT excluded — there the transports involve both generators and the eigenvector property fails; that case remains scope-(a) open.

'sorry-free != derived' seam: the step d_q sigma_i = ds_i is entrywise differentiation done by hand (sympy checks it here; Lean takes ds_i as supplied data). Everything downstream of it is machine-checked.
Every symbolic result is q-INDEPENDENT, so the q0 pin does not affect the conclusion; the experimental proton anchor is recorded for layer purity.
q0AnchorReason: recovered by transcription from this witness's own payload (key(s): parameters.q0_experimental_proton_anchor). No producer was re-run and no number changed; the pin was always recorded, under a non-canonical key.
